editorial:
Imagine you are watching a high-stakes game of cat and mouse where the killer is always one step ahead of everyone. You follow a smart psychologist who loves studying how criminals think, and he ends up helping the police solve a series of strange murders. The vibe is dark and tense, making you feel the pressure the cops are under as they struggle to find any real clues. It does not rely on cheap jumpscares but instead builds a slow sense of dread that keeps you glued to your seat throughout the whole story.

What really makes this work is the acting and the way the mystery unfolds. The twists are genuinely surprising and not easy to guess, which is rare for these kinds of movies. While some parts move a bit slowly in the middle, the payoff at the end is totally worth it. If you enjoy a good puzzle, you should definitely check this out. It looks great in high quality, so I suggest streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV for the best experience. You could even add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you love owning top-tier thrillers.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that the killer is actually a police officer who had a grudge against the victims. He used his position and knowledge of the law to hide his tracks and trick the investigators. After a tense final showdown, the psychologist uses his skills to figure out the killer's pattern and expose him. The movie ends with the killer finally being caught and the police realizing they had the murderer right under their noses the whole time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves detective stories and unexpected plot twists.
